Concurrency substrate for Boogie stores, built on a Disruptor-style ring buffer (threading-first; ARC required for concurrent stores).

When a store is constructed with enableConcurrency = true it owns a ConcurrentState[T]:

  • a WriteRing[Queued[T]]: a pre-allocated, power-of-two ring of task slots with sequence barriers (claim -> write -> ordered publish). Producers claim via an atomic, write the task with Nim move semantics, and publish the cursor contiguously via CAS - so a published sequence is the single authoritative signal and lost wakeups are structurally impossible.
  • one consumer thread that drains the ring in order: it applies each task under the target table's write lock, appends to the store WAL (group commit), and bumps that table's appliedSeq for synchronous visibility.
  • a metaMu RWLock guarding the table registry and a walLock serializing WAL appends.

Every table/collection gets a TableSlot[T] (embedded as a field): mu (RWLock) gives unlimited concurrent readers; the appliedSeq generation barrier gives synchronous visibility to writers. The slot's owner is an opaque pointer to the owning table, used only while dropped is false.

Write tasks carry value-type data only (no shared refs); the ring moves them with correct refcounting (unlike a channel's raw memcpy).

Imports

wal

Types

ConcurrentState[T] = ref object
Store-level concurrency state. nil when the store is created without enableConcurrency. 
Queued[T] = object
A submitted write op: the target table's slot, its per-table order, and the op payload. 
RwLock = object
Readers-writer lock. Multiple readers can acquire the lock at the same time, but only one writer can acquire the lock at a time. 
TableSlot[T] = ref object
  mu*: RwLock
  owner*: pointer
Per-table/collection concurrency state. 
WriteRing[T] = ref object
Disruptor-style ring buffer with sequence barriers. Producers claim a slot via nextClaim, write the task, and publish the cursor contiguously via CAS (a plain store could regress it). The consumer reads the cursor and drains in order.

proc appendWal[T](cc: ConcurrentState[T]; wal: var Wal; entry: WalEntry;

Appends one WAL entry under the store's WAL lock, flushing in a group commit once flushEvery entries are pending (async durability).

Stops the consumer thread and performs a final WAL flush. 
proc consume[T](r: WriteRing[T]; onTask: proc (x: T) {.closure, ...gcsafe.}) {.
    ...gcsafe.}
Consumer loop: waits for the cursor to advance, drains published slots in order, and advances the gating sequence (waking producers blocked on a full ring). Runs until stop is called.

    ...gcsafe.}; ctx: pointer): ConcurrentState[T]
proc newTableSlot[T](owner: pointer): TableSlot[T]
Creates an unarmed per-table slot. owner is an opaque pointer to the owning table/collection, dereferenced by the store's apply only while the slot is not dropped. 
proc newWriteRing[T](capacityPower = 10): WriteRing[T]
Creates a ring with 2^capacityPower pre-allocated slots (power of two). 
proc stop[T](r: WriteRing[T])
proc submit[T](cc: ConcurrentState[T]; slot: TableSlot[T]; op: sink T): uint64
Enqueues op for the given table and returns its per-table sequence number. The caller should then waitApplied for synchronous visibility. 
proc submit[T](r: WriteRing[T]; task: sink T): int64 {....gcsafe.}
Claims a slot, waits for space (backpressure), writes the task, and publishes it. Returns the sequence number. 
proc waitApplied[T](slot: TableSlot[T]; order: uint64)
Blocks until the op with the given per-table sequence has been applied to the in-memory state (synchronous visibility). Durability (WAL flush) is async.
